newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed slightly on Thursday as reaction buys followed a sudden selling wave sparked by political developments in early afternoon trade, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at a third consecutive all-time high of 1,180, up two points, or 0.17 percent from Wednesday's previous record of 1,178. In dollar terms, it was unchanged from yesterday's record of 1.05 cents.

The index dived to a low of 1,165 in the afternoon from an earlier high of 1,197 on sales prompted by Turkish far right party the BBP saying it was withdrawing its support from the country's Islamist-led coalition, cutting its majority in parliament to a handful of votes.
The index recovered on reaction buys towards the close.
"The BBP statement saying it was withdrawing its support from the coalition was used as an excuse because a down correction was long overdue," said Kadri Isk from Halkbank.
Trade volume surged to 26.30 trillion lira ($234.3 million) from Wednesday's 20.17 trillion ($179.5 million) due to sharp fluctuations in the day.

Three-day gains totalled 3.9 percent since Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the latest uptrend boosted by lower money and bond market rates, a quiet dollar and 1996 profit prospects of companies since the beginning of 1997.
The index had surged 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consequtive days after the market reopened on January 2, following a five-day holiday.
